body:
<!-- app-notice
level: important
text: Fixes for the first-boot crash on phones with Cortex-A55 class cores, the iOS 16 start on Android 10, and setups that stalled or stopped at 98 %. A setup that failed before can be started again from Set up.
text: On chips whose timer is not 19.2 MHz (Dimensity and others) iOS now gets the right clock. A quick save made before on such a phone is not loaded: the next start is a cold boot.
text: Experimental: a phone without an Adreno whose own graphics driver passes the GPU check can now try iOS 26 and watchOS on it. We could not test this ourselves; please send a report either way.
text: After iOS has run for ten minutes the app may ask whether to add your phone to the list of tested phones.
-->
**New engines for the first time since 0.1.2, with fixes for crashes and stalls on phones we do not own. Most of them could only be tested on our one phone: please tell us what changed on yours.**

## Engines

- **First boot on CPUs without SSBS.** iOS 26 and watchOS panicked or aborted at their first boot on phones with Cortex-A55 class cores (#18, #42, #57). Fixed in the engine; on our phone both the normal path and a forced "no SSBS" boot reach the lock screen. Never run on a real A55 phone.
- **iOS 16 on Android 10.** The start was killed with signal 31, because Android 10 forbids a system call the engine made (#23). The engines no longer make it on kernels older than 6.1. Never run on Android 10.
- **QEMU ending during DataMigration or after a long run.** The engine could use up Android's limit of memory mappings (#6, #10). It now maps the guest's surfaces only when they are used.
- **A screen that ended QEMU.** A drawing path with an extended-range colour target was refused and took QEMU down (#11).
- **Very slow picture on some Mali phones.** Reading a frame back took about 250 ms where the GPU's memory is not cached for the CPU (#66). Frames are now read through a cached buffer there. Our phone does not take this path, so it has never run on a Mali or PowerVR.
- **Adreno 825** (Snapdragon 8s Gen 4) is in the driver's table (#4). Nobody has run it yet.

## Setup

- **The right clock on every chip.** iOS was told the timer runs at 19.2 MHz. That is true for Snapdragons; a Dimensity 9500 runs it at 1 GHz, so the guest's clock ran 52 times too fast (#66). The app now reads the frequency from the CPU, and measures it where the CPU does not say (an Exynos 9810 answers 0; measured on a Galaxy S9+: 26 MHz). A quick save made with another frequency is not loaded.
- **iOS 26: a shorter first boot.** One of iOS's migration plug-ins did nothing useful here and took about a third of the DataMigration boot; it stays out of the disk now (helps #16, #48, #55, #65).
- **iOS 26: "the guest did not answer sync" at 98 %** (#19, #37, #50): a setup boot now also ends cleanly when the guest's shell has gone quiet.
- **Waits follow signs of life instead of a fixed limit.** The iOS 16 first start gave up after a flat 2 hours and the iOS 26 DataMigration after a flat 3 (#59, #23, #16, #55, #65). They now go on while the guest shows progress, stop after an hour in which nothing at all moves, and keep the console's last lines for a report. When the setup does give up, iOS is saved and closed first, so Resume carries on from there; 0.1.5 left iOS 16 running in the background, where Android later closed the app (#84). An iOS 26 boot whose programs keep restarting is given two hours: on our own phone such a stretch ended by itself after 26 minutes and the setup finished.
- **Why a setup is on hold.** The screen and the notification say whether it waits for the phone to cool down or for the charger (battery under 15 %); #63 was the battery rule under a "hot" text. Holds start later (thermal "severe") and end at "moderate".
- **Low memory.** When Android closes the app for memory during a build, the next run gives the helper VM one size less (#54, #67), and a start or a setup with little free memory asks first (#8, #17). Why the copy is so slow on those phones is not known yet.
- A notification that Android refuses no longer takes the setup or iOS down with it (#43).
- The app opens on home; Set up is one section per system.

## Running

- **Install an .ipa into iOS 26** from the phone ("Install an .ipa…" under iOS 26 on home). The app signs it ad hoc and puts it onto iOS 26's disk while iOS is off, so the next start is a boot, not a quick-save load. Not every app runs.
- **GPU check:** it no longer asks for 16-bit storage buffers (more Adreno 600-series pass, in compatibility mode); a GPU that is not supported yet gets a plain text and the link to its family's issue (#22, #31, #51, #62, #64). On drivers whose shared memory needs cache syncs (newer Malis) its host-memory test now does them, so it no longer reports that memory as broken there (#81; the fix is @fasilfaezi's, #82).
- **Experimental: iOS 26 and watchOS on the phone's own graphics driver.** Until now only Adreno phones could pass, because the engine always used the app's own Turnip driver. A phone without an Adreno now passes when its own Vulkan driver gets every test of the check right and lacks only sparse memory binding: iOS 26 and watchOS then start on that driver, in the compatibility mode. This is how @fasilfaezi booted iOS 26 on a Mali-G1-Ultra with this engine (#66, #81). We have no such phone, so it has never run in our hands: expect a slow picture, wrong pictures in places (the engine does not do the cache syncs such a driver needs) or a stop, and send the report from Logs either way. The check's screen says "experimental" when this is the route. Nothing changes on Adreno phones.
- **Reports** name the decisive line, memory-mapping exhaustion, a phone maker's battery manager, and Android 12's limit on child processes (#53, #58, #66). The same report is not opened twice a day. A run that ended for another reason in its first minutes is no longer reported as the memory-mapping limit (the engine names that limit at every start, and the app took that for the cause).
- **"Works" report.** When iOS has run for ten minutes and your chip is not on the list of [tested phones](https://github.com/alpersamur3/asoft-ios-android/blob/main/DEVICES.md), home shows one line that opens a filled-in GitHub issue with the phone's chip, the start time and the frame rate. You read it and send it, or not; the app sends nothing by itself.
- The live view is rebuilt for the system that runs (the watch was drawn full width after iOS 26).

## Not fixed

- Mali and PowerVR GPUs without `VK_EXT_external_memory_host` and Samsung Xclipse still cannot run iOS 26 and watchOS (#22, #51, #62, #64, [asoft-ios #4](https://github.com/alpersamur3/asoft-ios/issues/4)). Newer Malis that do have it can try the experimental route above; making it fast and correct there (cache syncs in the engine, a quicker way to show the picture) is the next work. iOS 16 runs without a GPU.
- iOS 26's DataMigration still stalls on some phones (#16, #55, #65): the cause is not known. This version shortens that boot, waits longer for one that may still come back, ends one that shows nothing sooner, and records more about it.
- The slow "copying iOS" on phones with little memory (#54, #67).

## Tested

On our Galaxy S25 Ultra (Snapdragon 8 Elite, Android 17): updating over 0.1.5 keeps iOS and loads its quick save; iOS 26 cold boot to the lock screen in about two minutes, Save and close, resume; iOS 16 start, save, resume; an iOS 16 setup from an IPSW that was already on the phone, to the end in 51 minutes (disk 20, first start 29); a full iOS 26 setup from Apple's files that were already on the phone, to the end in 99 minutes (disk 31, DataMigration 45 with a long silent stretch that it came out of by itself), then its first boot to the home screen, Save and close, and a resume in 6 seconds. On a Galaxy S9+ (Exynos 9810, Mali-G72, Android 10): the app opens, the GPU check says in plain words why iOS 26 will not run there, the timer is measured as 26 MHz; no iOS was booted on it. Also on the S25: the "works" report with a test list (line, dialog, both buttons); the low-memory question before a start. The experimental own-driver route was forced on the S25 in a debug build: the engine opened Android's Vulkan loader and Qualcomm's driver, refused that driver by name (it lacks the shared-memory extension, so it would never pass the check) and the app said so; iOS 26 on a driver that passes has never run in our hands. Not run by us: the download steps, and everything above that says so.

0.1.6 installs over 0.1.5 and earlier and keeps your iOS, its settings and its saves (same signing key). If the APK will not install, download it again and compare `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

Signing certificate SHA-256: `d412a33bde757a6b36524e09c215b1e2a2a21285b0fd38e8e30a8c5f23672ef2`. Sources and licenses as in 0.1.2 (the app's README).
